deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is axiomatizing arrangements of pseudo-lines in the projective plane by local combinatorial data. The data are a cell complex K, at each vertex s the set I_s of pseudo-lines through s (with ν_s = card I_s), and the set of oriented pseudo-lines. The aim is to say when such an 'oriented covering' comes from a genuine 2-dimensional arrangement.

Previous page. An oriented pseudo-line Δ not through s cuts the lines through s in an order. This gives a generator u_{s,Δ} of a cyclic group Z_s acting on I_s, namely the cyclic order of the pencil at s. Grothendieck then lifts u_{s,Δ} to a permutation ū_{s,Δ} of the doubled set Ī_s of the 2ν_s oriented lines through s (the half-rays at s). He requires the lift to be a circular permutation, which leaves 2^{ν_s−1} a priori choices.

This page, first part. The lift is fixed geometrically. Take D through s, its successor D' (the next line of the pencil met by Δ), and the triangle with sides Δ, D, D'. The orientation of D' is the one for which the three edges a (s→t), b (s→u) and c (t→u, oriented by Δ) are related as follows: Δ's orientation is opposite to the boundary orientation of the triangle W_{i,j,k}. This determines the sense of D' from those of Δ and D.

(A2). This prescription, with s and Δ fixed, yields a circular permutation ū_{s,Δ} of the 2ν_s oriented lines lying over u_{s,Δ}. Its ν_s-th power is a priori either the identity or the 'non-diagonal' (antipodal) involution of (26). Axiom A2 requires it to be the antipodal involution, flipping every orientation. This is the projective, Möbius-type feature: turning half-way round the pencil reverses each line.

N.B. / (30). Reversing Δ inverts the permutation: ū_{s,−Δ} = ū_{s,Δ}^{−1}. The pair Z_{s,Δ} = {ū_{s,Δ}, ū_{s,−Δ}} is a subset of the symmetric group on Ī_s.

(A3). For any other pseudo-line Δ' not through s, Z_{s,Δ'} = Z_{s,Δ}, written Z_s. So the oriented cyclic structure at s is independent of the transversal, up to inversion.

These conditions hold for coverings coming from actual 2-dimensional arrangements. Next page: this gives a surjection from oriented lines not through s onto Z_s, compatible with ±1. Grothendieck then requires compatibility along each edge a = ss' of K (axiom A9). In effect he builds a combinatorial 'local system' of cyclic orientation data on the 1-skeleton.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The statement 'Δ' another pseudo-line passing through s' in (A3) must mean NOT passing through s, as in the definitions; this is likely a slip or a misreading of 'ne passant pas'.
The count 2^{ν_s−1} and the claim that the triangle prescription gives a circular permutation are asserted, not proved, on this page; they are then imposed as axiom A2.

ideas.what: Encoding a pseudo-line arrangement by local cyclic orders. At each crossing s, any transversal oriented pseudo-line induces the cyclic order of the pencil; this is lifted to the 2ν half-rays with u^ν = antipodal map.
ideas.modern_name: Local sequences / allowable sequences; local cyclic structure of rank-3 oriented matroids (chirotopes)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Goodman–Pollack (allowable sequences, ~1980–84); Folkman–Lawrence (1978) and Bland–Las Vergnas for oriented matroids

ideas.what: Axiom that the cyclic data at s is independent of the transversal, up to inversion, with inversion under orientation reversal (eq. 30, A3).
ideas.modern_name: Consistency of the pencil's cyclic order (rank-2 contractions of a rank-3 oriented matroid)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Oriented matroid theory (contraction at a point)

ideas.what: Fixing the orientation of the successor line through the boundary orientation of the triangle formed with the transversal.
ideas.modern_name: Chirotope sign of a triple / triangle orientation in a pseudo-line arrangement

missed.claim: Grothendieck independently develops a local, gluing-style axiomatization of projective pseudo-line arrangements. The local data at each vertex are cyclic groups Z_s of oriented-pencil rotations, transported along edges (A9 on the next page); in effect a covering/local-system viewpoint. This parallels oriented-matroid and allowable-sequence theory but is phrased as descent data on the 1-skeleton. It is an undocumented chapter of his post-1981 combinatorial work, not a new theorem.
missed.quote: (A2) Cette prescription ... est bien une permutation circulaire ... (A3) ... Z_{s,Δ'} = Z_{s,Δ} (dit Z_s)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Of historical interest: it documents Grothendieck working on combinatorial models of real plane arrangements, presumably tied to his 'tame topology' and anabelian interests. Mathematically it seems subsumed by the Folkman–Lawrence topological representation theorem.

deep.surprise_reason: These are careful but standard local axioms for pseudo-line arrangements (cyclic pencil orders, antipodal half-turn), largely known from oriented matroid theory. The novelty is only biographical and in the local-system style of the formulation.
transcription_corrections: The margin note reads roughly 'i.e. l'orientation qu'ils bordent ... triangles'. The main text likely reads 'opposée à l'orientation des triangles W_{i,j,k} de sommets pss. droites Δ, D, D''.
'au sens des C permutations u_{s,Δ}' is likely 'au-dessus de la permutation u_{s,Δ} de I_s'.
'AB On a' is likely 'NB On a'.
'(dit Z_s)' may be '(soit Z_s)'. The Z symbols are Gothic letters carrying arrows.
In (A3) the text likely says Δ' is another pseudo-line 'ne passant pas par s' (the line is cramped). The struck-out first attempt at (A3) mentions Δ'.
'C' in the (30) line is a script S for the symmetric group S_{I_s} (𝔖_{I_s}).
